task: Get a reminder to call the camp director about Rafi's waitlist, and see whether the app can help you follow up with the camp.
transcript: Opened the app and saw a Home screen asking 'What can I help with?' with example requests and a note that nothing is sent without my OK.
Typed 'Remind me to call the camp director about Rafi's waitlist tomorrow morning' into the box and tapped Send.
The screen switched to a conversation titled 'Remind you to call camp director tomorrow' showing 'Your family admin helper is on it' and 'Working on it'.

After about 45 seconds it answered: reminder set for tomorrow, Sat Nov 14 at 9am, to call Marcy Feld at Camp Kaylie, with her phone number (845) 555-0142 and where things stand (Rafi #4 on the Session 2 waitlist as of Oct 20; I emailed her Nov 1 and she has not replied).
Typed 'can you help me follow up with her? she never answered my email' and tapped Send.
Saw 'Working on it' for about 2 minutes; after a minute or so it added 'Reading email and calendar can take a few minutes', which reassured me.

A draft email appeared labelled 'Draft email, not sent', To marcy@campkaylie.test, Subject 'Re: Rafi Levin - Session 2 waitlist', with Open in Mail and Copy buttons and a polite follow-up message signed Dana.
Open in Mail would hand the draft to my own mail app, so I stopped there and closed the app.
stumbles: The follow-up draft took about 2 minutes with only dots on screen at first; ChatGPT answers faster. The 'can take a few minutes' note helped.
The draft offers to be 'flexible on dates', which is a little odd since the session dates are fixed, but easy to edit.
The conversation title still says 'Remind you to call camp director tomorrow' even after it became an email draft, a small mismatch.
My reminder is described in the reply, but I did not see it listed anywhere else to double-check it was saved.
verdict: I typed two plain sentences and got a 9am reminder with Marcy's number and a ready follow-up email that was clearly marked as not sent. It felt almost like ChatGPT, only slower on the email and a bit vague about where the reminder lives.
